chains.title: Possible GATA2-mediated regulation of LMO1
chains.element: The variant-containing distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E1518342

links.claim: GATA2 occupies the variant site and is highly expressed in SK-N-SH, making it a candidate TF. The proposed direction is stronger binding to A, but this is an unsubstantiated hypothesis: no allele-specific QBiC-SELEX result or other evidence establishes whether C or A binds more strongly. GATA2 is weakly prioritized over the alternatives by its expression and occupancy, not by demonstrated allele-specific binding.
The variant lies in a distal enhancer-like cCRE. Its reported activity scores are maxima across biosamples, not SK-N-SH-specific evidence of enhancer activity.

LMO1 is a plausible target because it is nearby and is the strongest Open Targets gene nomination at this variant, but direct regulation of LMO1 by this cCRE is not established. The A-associated decrease in LMO1 expression reported in skeletal muscle does not determine the effect in SK-N-SH.
GATA2 occupancy at the site is reported in SK-N-SH, the expression-context cell line, although this does not show an allele-dependent effect.

LMO1 has independent neuroblastoma disease and literature support, including reports connecting its overexpression to pro-metastatic properties. These data do not connect this variant or GATA2 to those effects; LMO1 is not a CRISPR dependency in SK-N-SH.

predictions: The working, unverified direction is greater GATA2 binding to A than C. The supplied evidence does not establish this direction.
If the variant acts through this chain, editing the allele will alter LMO1 expression in SK-N-SH, and that effect will depend on GATA2.
falsified_if: Sensitive allele-specific assays find no GATA2 binding difference at the site or find stronger binding to C.
Allele editing does not change LMO1 expression, or any expression effect persists unchanged when GATA2 is perturbed.

matrix.test: Compare C- and A-containing site oligonucleotides in SK-N-SH nuclear extract by EMSA, with TF-specific supershift or antibody disruption for GATA2, GATA3, and TEAD4.

outcomes.outcome: No reproducible allele-dependent shift attributable to one of the proposed TFs.
A reproducible C/A binding difference attributable to GATA2; the chain's working direction predicts stronger binding to A.
A reproducible C/A binding difference attributable to GATA3; the chain's working direction predicts stronger binding to A.
A reproducible C/A binding difference attributable to TEAD4; the chain's working direction predicts stronger binding to A.

matrix.test: Use isogenic SK-N-SH cells edited C-to-A and A-to-C; measure allele-dependent TF occupancy at the site and LMO1 expression, with separate perturbation of GATA2, GATA3, and TEAD4.

outcomes.outcome: No reproducible allele-dependent occupancy and LMO1 expression effect attributable to these TFs.
An allele-dependent GATA2 occupancy difference accompanies an LMO1 expression change that is reduced by GATA2 perturbation.
An allele-dependent GATA3 occupancy difference accompanies an LMO1 expression change that is reduced by GATA3 perturbation.
An allele-dependent TEAD4 occupancy difference accompanies an LMO1 expression change that is reduced by TEAD4 perturbation.

matrix.test: Test whether the variant-containing cCRE regulates LMO1 using targeted CRISPRi of the cCRE and measure LMO1 expression in SK-N-SH.

outcomes.outcome: No reproducible effect of cCRE perturbation on LMO1 expression.
The cCRE perturbation changes LMO1 expression; this test alone does not establish GATA2 mediation or an allele effect.
The cCRE perturbation changes LMO1 expression; this test alone does not establish GATA3 mediation or an allele effect.
The cCRE perturbation changes LMO1 expression; this test alone does not establish TEAD4 mediation or an allele effect.

next_experiment: Start with the low-cost EMSA using C- and A-containing oligonucleotides and SK-N-SH nuclear extract, with TF-specific supershift or antibody disruption. A reproducible GATA2-attributable allelic difference would support H2 over the top-ranked null; the working prediction is stronger binding to A, but the supplied evidence does not establish that direction. No difference would weaken H2, though a negative in-vitro result would not rule out a chromatin-dependent effect.
